::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Epiphany [6 January 1894?][^1]  
**From:** Elderfield Otterbourne Winchester  
**Manuscript:** MS Bodleian Library, Oxford: MS English Letters: e.174 ff 164
:::

Dear [Mr Bullock](people/person_221.qmd),
I did not think much could be done with his times in France, as they generally did not proceed from St Denys’ foundation but I took a different line, which I hope may suit you. Only can you fill in the name of the seventh Champion of Christendom[.] I think he was of Portugal, but I cannot remember, I wish he was St Maurice of Germany, but I fear he was not[^2]

Yours truly
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: Dated by the reference to St. Maurice in the letter of 19 March 1894 below.
[^2]: The Seven Champions of Christendom were the seven national saints of England, Scotland, Ireland, Wales, France, Spain and Italy: Saints George, Andrew, Patrick, David, Denis, James and Anthony.  St. Moritz or Maurice was a Roman legionary martyred *c*.285 whose cult was important in southern Germany and Italy.  The work CMY was doing was associated with Bullock's *Daily Lections* project.
